item.research_question: How does thermal shock (annealing at 400–800 °C) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and tribocorrosion resistance of strongly amorphous AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy films in extreme service environments?
item.material_system: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film (composition: 15.82 at.% Al, 22.86 at.% Cr, 19.49 at.% Ti, 24.74 at.% Zr, 17.09 at.% Mo) deposited on 304 stainless steel and silicon wafers
item.processing_route: Co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) using Ti50Mo50, pure Al, Cr, and Zr targets; substrate sputtered at −800, −600, and −400 V for 45 s; annealed in air at 400 °C, 600 °C, and 800 °C for 1 h
item.test_conditions: High-temperature oxidation in air at 800 °C for 1 h; tribocorrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution with Si3N4 ceramic balls (Φ 6 mm) at 5 N load, 1 Hz frequency for 50 min (10–40 min loading phase)
key_findings: After annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer formed with a thickness of 5.47 μm and oxygen content of 20.50 at.%
Hardness (H) and Young's modulus (E) reached maximum values of 20.88 GPa and 220.2 GPa, respectively, after annealing at 800 °C
The H/E ratio and H3/E2 ratio for the 800 °C annealed film were 0.0948 and 0.1877, respectively, indicating superior crack and plastic deformation resistance
The film annealed at 800 °C exhibited the lowest tribocorrosion metrics: ΔOCP = 0.055, COF = 0.04, and wear rate = 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1
Annealing at 400 °C and 600 °C resulted in no oxide particles and minimal changes in film thickness or morphology
The amorphous structure at 600 °C led to increased hardness (14.97 GPa) and modulus (176.1 GPa) due to relaxation, while 800 °C added dispersion strengthening from oxide precipitates
item.mechanism: Zr and Ti elements preferentially oxidize to form ZrO2 and TiO2; competitive oxidation-reduction reactions occur where TiO2 is reduced by Zr, leading to the accumulation of oxides that polymerize into stable ZrTiO4 spinel; this dense composite oxide layer acts as a barrier preventing further oxidation, while the fine oxide particles provide dispersion strengthening to enhance mechanical properties and tribocorrosion resistance.
quotes: the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing
the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties
Zr and Ti elements are preferentially oxidized to form ZrO2 and TiO2. Meanwhile, metal elements that form low free energy oxides can undergo reduction reactions with oxides with high free energy.

records.text: Paper card. Question: How does thermal shock (annealing at 400–800 °C) affect the microstructure, mechanical properties, and tribocorrosion resistance of strongly amorphous AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy films in extreme service environments?. System: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film (composition: 15.82 at.% Al, 22.86 at.% Cr, 19.49 at.% Ti, 24.74 at.% Zr, 17.09 at.% Mo) deposited on 304 stainless steel and silicon wafers. Processing: Co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) using Ti50Mo50, pure Al, Cr, and Zr targets; substrate sputtered at −800, −600, and −400 V for 45 s; annealed in air at 400 °C, 600 °C, and 800 °C for 1 h. Test conditions: High-temperature oxidation in air at 800 °C for 1 h; tribocorrosion in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution with Si3N4 ceramic balls (Φ 6 mm) at 5 N load, 1 Hz frequency for 50 min (10–40 min loading phase). Findings: After annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer formed with a thickness of 5.47 μm and oxygen content of 20.50 at.%; Hardness (H) and Young's modulus (E) reached maximum values of 20.88 GPa and 220.2 GPa, respectively, after annealing at 800 °C; The H/E ratio and H3/E2 ratio for the 800 °C annealed film were 0.0948 and 0.1877, respectively, indicating superior crack and plastic deformation resistance; The film annealed at 800 °C exhibited the lowest tribocorrosion metrics: ΔOCP = 0.055, COF = 0.04, and wear rate = 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1; Annealing at 400 °C and 600 °C resulted in no oxide particles and minimal changes in film thickness or morphology; The amorphous structure at 600 °C led to increased hardness (14.97 GPa) and modulus (176.1 GPa) due to relaxation, while 800 °C added dispersion strengthening from oxide precipitates. Mechanism: Zr and Ti elements preferentially oxidize to form ZrO2 and TiO2; competitive oxidation-reduction reactions occur where TiO2 is reduced by Zr, leading to the accumulation of oxides that polymerize into stable ZrTiO4 spinel; this dense composite oxide layer acts as a barrier preventing further oxidation, while the fine oxide particles provide dispersion strengthening to enhance mechanical properties and tribocorrosion resistance.. Quote: "the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing"
